questions.title: ANP inhibits sodium reabsorption (source paper A)
questions.subject: renal
questions.module_subject: SCU-FBS102 > Physiology > Renal Physiology > Sodium Regulation
questions.question: Which of the following acts is a primary physiological function performed by the atrial natriuretic peptide (ANP) hormone?

explanations.A: Incorrect. ANP does not stimulate ADH secretion; if anything, its overall effect (promoting sodium and water loss) works against ADH's water-retaining action, not alongside it.
explanations.B: Incorrect. ANP suppresses, rather than stimulates, renin secretion, consistent with its role as a counterweight to the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system.
explanations.C: Incorrect. ANP promotes, not inhibits, water excretion, because the water that follows the unreabsorbed sodium it causes to be excreted is also lost in the urine.
explanations.D: Correct. ANP is secreted by atrial myocytes in response to atrial stretch from a rising central blood volume, and it acts on the renal collecting duct to inhibit sodium reabsorption, increasing sodium (and secondarily water) loss in the urine. This natriuretic action is the direct physiological opposite of aldosterone, and together with ANP's vasodilating and renin-suppressing effects it lowers blood volume and blood pressure.

questions.learning_objective: State that atrial natriuretic peptide inhibits renal sodium reabsorption (promoting natriuresis), and that this is the physiological opposite of aldosterone's sodium-retaining action.

questions.title: ANP inhibits sodium reabsorption (source paper B)
questions.subject: renal
questions.module_subject: SCU-FBS102 > Physiology > Renal Physiology > Sodium Regulation
questions.question: Which of the following is a direct physiological function of the atrial natriuretic peptide (ANP) hormone?

explanations.A: Incorrect. ANP does not stimulate ADH secretion; its net effect promotes fluid loss rather than fluid retention, the opposite direction from ADH's own action.
explanations.B: Incorrect. ANP suppresses renin secretion rather than stimulating it, fitting its role as the physiological opposite of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system.
explanations.C: Incorrect. ANP promotes water excretion rather than inhibiting it, since water follows the sodium that ANP causes the kidney to excrete.
explanations.D: Correct. ANP acts directly on the renal collecting duct to inhibit sodium reabsorption, driving natriuresis; because this response is triggered by atrial stretch from increased central blood volume, it functions as a direct brake on blood volume and blood pressure whenever the atria sense overfilling. This natriuretic action is the direct physiological opposite of aldosterone's sodium-retaining effect on the same nephron segment.

questions.learning_objective: State that atrial natriuretic peptide inhibits renal sodium reabsorption (promoting natriuresis), and that this is the physiological opposite of aldosterone's sodium-retaining action.
